open_points.subject: Agent-visible failure details
open_points.text: A `failure_detail` whose class is above `open` ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class.
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 byte length
Unicode code-point length
Length of the bounded stored detail rather than the original detail
open_points.default_guess: UTF-8 byte length of the bounded stored detail

open_points.subject: Credential trailing newline
open_points.text: its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value
open_points.question: What exactly counts as the one removable trailing newline, and what happens with CRLF or multiple trailing newline characters?
options: Remove one final LF only
Remove one final LF or CRLF sequence
Strip all trailing newline sequences
open_points.default_guess: Remove one final LF, leaving any preceding CR or additional newline to fail the control-character check

open_points.subject: Credential header serialization
open_points.text: its content decoded as UTF-8 ... is the value ... A resolved value is added as that header.
open_points.question: Are non-ASCII credential values allowed, and if so, how are they encoded into the HTTP header field value?
options: Require printable ASCII and refuse anything else
Encode the Unicode value as UTF-8 header bytes
Use the HTTP client's header encoding
open_points.default_guess: Require printable ASCII and report `credential_unresolved` otherwise

open_points.subject: MCP listen address
open_points.text: the address the kernel's one `mcp` entrance listens on
open_points.question: What forms of listen address are valid, and does an invalid or unbindable address refuse startup under a defined condition?
options: A host-and-port value with startup refusal on invalid or unbindable input
A Unix-socket path
An implementation-defined transport address
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit host and port and refuse startup if it is invalid or cannot be bound

open_points.subject: Selected manifest instance name
open_points.text: the selected manifest instance name of each service it selects one for ... The instance of every service is the one the installation selects
open_points.question: What happens when configuration names an instance that does not exist in the configured manifest revision: does the kernel refuse startup, treat the service as having no selected instance, or fail only requests to that service?
options: Refuse kernel startup
Treat it as no selected instance
Start and fail only that service's proposals and sends
open_points.default_guess: Start and treat the service as having no selected instance, so its bindings and sends are refused

open_points.subject: Waiting elements during advancement
open_points.text: A waiting element can still execute, so M19's "no node can run any more" holds only when nothing waits
open_points.question: Can an element waiting for approval, service availability, or unknown-outcome resolution execute during ordinary advancement before the event that ends its wait?
options: No; it remains ineligible until the specified approval, resume, or resolution
Yes; it remains executable despite its waiting point
open_points.default_guess: No; the word `can` is treated as an error and waiting prevents execution

open_points.subject: Validation of several node inputs
open_points.text: A value is validated against the source port when it is produced and against the target port before it enters a node; a violation concludes the producing node, or the receiving node, `contract_violation`
open_points.question: When values for several input ports violate their target ports, in what order are they checked and which violation supplies the recorded failure detail?
options: Input-port name order by Unicode code point
Edge delivery order
Record all violations in one bounded detail
open_points.default_guess: Input-port name order by Unicode code point, recording the first violation

open_points.subject: Ready nodes versus newly non-executable nodes
open_points.text: The next node is the ready node with the smallest `node_id` ... An input port that can no longer receive a value ... makes its node `skipped_by_guard` ... A node an input of which comes from a failed node ... concludes `upstream_failed`
open_points.question: When a request simultaneously has ready nodes and nodes that can now be concluded `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed`, which conclusions are recorded first and how are they interleaved with executable nodes?
options: Resolve all skips and upstream failures first, then select a ready node
Compare executable and non-executable nodes together by `node_id`
Execute ready nodes first and derive non-executable nodes only when no ready node remains
open_points.default_guess: Repeatedly resolve all determinable non-executable nodes in `node_id` order before selecting the smallest ready node

open_points.subject: Oversized aggregate output of a mapped node
open_points.text: a list whose canonical bytes exceed `stored_value_bytes_max` is not written: the node is then failed for its dependants ... No record of the node states that failure: like the list, it is derived from the elements' records and `stored_value_bytes_max`
open_points.question: What exact status, reason, and failure detail do run and trace readers report for this derived mapped-node failure, given that no NodeExecution records it?
options: Derived `contract_violation` with `value_too_large`
Derived `resource_exhausted`
Only a generic failed-node conclusion with no detail
